sections.html: Synodontis arnoulti Roman, 1966. Size: 101 mm (4 inches) SL. FishBase also lists 136 mm TL. IUCN Red List status: Vulnerable.
Africa: Volta basin. Type locality: Kou R., tributary of the Black Volta R., 30 km north of Bobo-Dioulasso, West Africa.

Lay the fish in your hand with its head toward your palm and the tail toward your fingers. Hold the dorsal spine between your middle and ring finger so the fish is belly up. The genital pore is in a small furrow of tissue (in healthy fish) and is obstructed by the pelvic fins. Pull down gently on the tail to arch the spine; the pelvic fins will stand and the furrow open to display the genital pore and the anus. The male has a somewhat ridged genital papilla with the spermatoduct on the back side, facing the tail fin. A gravid female also shows an extended papilla, but the oviduct is on the ventral side of the papilla (and may show a little redness if really gravid). A thin or emaciated female will have just two pink pores, the oviduct and the anus.
Breeding: unreported. There is no breeding report.

All species in the genus Synodontis have a hardened head cap with an attached process (humeral process) situated behind the gill opening and pointing posteriorly. The dorsal and pectoral fins have a hardened, serrated first ray. The caudal fin is always forked. There is one pair of maxillary barbels, sometimes with membranes and occasionally branched. The two pairs of mandibular barbels are often branched and can have nodes. The cone-shaped teeth in the upper jaw are short; those in the lower jaw are S-shaped and movable. These fish produce audible sounds when disturbed by rubbing the base of the pectoral spine against the pectoral girdle.
Ann. Mus. R. Afr. Cent. Ser. 8 Zool.No. 150 - pp141 - Pl. 7 (fig. 14)
